items.summary:
Los Angeles Rams running back Kyren Williams acknowledged that his quarterback, Matthew Stafford , has undergone a noticeable glow-up.  

“He’s looking good,” Williams, 26, exclusively told Us about Stafford, 38, via his partnership with Invisalign. “He’s like a fine wine.” 

In addition to Matthew’s increasingly youthful physical appearance, Williams explained how the quarterback’s love for his wife, Kelly , and their four daughters positively influences the entire organization. 

“It’s so cool because not only do you see them on game days, you also see them throughout the week,” Williams said of the Stafford family. “Sometimes they’ll be in the facility. I remember one time I was working out — it was such a cool moment, I told my whole family about it — I was working out one morning and he and his family were there shooting a podcast for the Rams. All of his daughters came up to me as I was working out and asked me questions and whatnot. I was like, ‘Man, that’s what it’s all about.’” 

Aaron Rodgers Goes Scorched Earth on 'Unwell' Mike McCarthy After Benching 

Matthew and Kelly, 37, share twins Sawyer and Chandler , 9, Hunter , 8 and Tyler , 6.  

“At the Rams, we’re a family,” Williams continued. “We’re family-oriented. That has allowed us to stay connected throughout even the hard times, throughout the rough start and the things that didn’t go our way.”

items.title: Melissa Joan Hart Explains Why She Had a 'Rough Time' on 'DWTS'
items.summary:
Melissa Joan Hart is recalling her “rough” experience on Dancing With the Stars season 9.

“I was there about six weeks. First time I had ever left my children,” Hart, 50, recalled in a Tuesday, November 24, Instagram video . “I wanted to be a dancer more than I wanted to be an actress, and so I was very excited about being on this show.”

Hart added that a friend told her to do the show and prove that she’s “not just the girl next door.”

“I did a good jive,” she recalled. “I’m really good at the Latin dances. I think my Charleston was so much fun. And here’s the thing: as an adult, I have been doing adult tap classes. The week I got kicked off, I was about to do a quickstep, and I think I would have killed that.”

Hart said she had chosen “The Bare Necessities” from Jungle Book as her song for her next dance because her sons were going to be in the ballroom during her live performance. (Hart shares Mason , 20, Braydon , 18, and Tucker, 14, with husband Mark Wilkerson .)

“But I got kicked off the week before because I had the flu. I was deathly ill,” she recalled. “I was trying to, like, be graceful, and I had the flu, and I was so sick. I really wanted to dance. I was very disappointed that I didn’t get to dance more, and I was also disappointed that I didn’t dance prettier than I did.”

TDOC officials told Pike’s legal team that she could no longer meet with the mental health expert that was hired to assist her in their case unless they were accompanied by one of Pike’s attorneys during the prison visit, according to a copy of the emergency motion viewed by People.

Pike’s lawyers said she was allowed to visit with the clinical psychologist for the first month after the failed lethal injection. On November 9, TDOC officials sent an email telling her counsel that she could only meet with the clinical psychologist if an “attorney of record” was present.

De Nino appeared on season 2 of Married at First Sight , which was filmed in 2014 and aired on Lifetime in 2015. The business owner was paired with law firm receptionist Jessica Castro . Though they had a tumultuous relationship, they ultimately chose to stay together at the end of the season.

items.title: Aaron Rodgers Goes Scorched Earth on 'Unwell' Mike McCarthy After Benching
items.summary:
Hours after he was shockingly benched by the Pittsburgh Steelers, Aaron Rodgers went on live TV to air his grievances — and he didn’t hold anything back.  

Rodgers, 42, appeared on ESPN’s The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday, November 25, where he accused Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy of falling asleep and snoring in team meetings, failing to watch game tape and confusing the Steelers and his former team, the Green Bay Packers, in a recent halftime speech.

“There’s no hyperbole, there’s no trying to stick it to you,” Rodgers said. “You’re unwell. What’s best for the team is you give it up to somebody and you take care of yourself and work on your health and do the schedule and do the team meetings.” 

Rodgers said concerns about McCarthy’s well-being have been a hot topic inside the Steelers building “for weeks and weeks and weeks.” 

Jordan Rodgers Breaks His Silence After Brother Aaron's Shocking Benching 

“Every time I bring these things up, he just denies it,” Rodgers argued. “There’s other individuals who’ve talked to him about some of these habits. He just shoots off at it and gets super angry.” 

The quarterback continued, “It’s been frustrating. The guys I talk to every single day share the same sentiment.” 

Rodgers recalled McCarthy’s halftime speech during the Steelers’ game against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, November 22, during which McCarthy, 63, allegedly confused the Steelers with the Packers, where he and Rodgers spent 13 seasons together.

While speaking to investigators, Gene allegedly said that the couple had gotten into an argument earlier that day about Christmas gifts for their children.

He was then arrested on Friday, November 20, and taken into custody. His bond hearing has not yet taken place, and the sheriff’s office said he will appear in court “at a later date.”
